quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #20
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: If you are driving in another driver's blind spot, what should you do?

options.text: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
Keep a steady pace.
Stay in the driver's blind spot.
Honk to let them know you are there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move forward or back so the other driver can see you.
questions.explanation: Do not drive in another driver's blind spot. Move forward or back so the driver can see you.

questions.question: If an oncoming driver is heading toward you in your lane, what should you do?

options.text: Honk, steer right, and speed up.
Honk, steer left, and brake.
Honk, steer right, and brake.
Stay in your lane, honk, and brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Honk, steer right, and brake.
questions.explanation: If another car is coming at you head-on, honk first to get their attention. If they do not move, steer right to escape. Do not steer left because if they correct at the last second, you will still crash. Brake hard and steady. Every mile per hour you slow down reduces the crash impact.

questions.question: When you see this sign, what does it mean?

options.text: There is an object on the roadway.
Traffic is coming from the right.
The road curves sharply to the left.
There is a merge point ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road curves sharply to the left.
questions.explanation: Chevron signs show a sharp curve in the direction the arrow points. In this case, the road curves sharply to the left. You may see several of these signs along the curve.

questions.question: If two drivers arrive at an open intersection at the same time, who has the right-of-way?

options.text: The driver on the right.
The driver on the left.
One driver may continue without stopping.
One driver should honk to show they are giving up the right-of-way.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver on the right.
questions.explanation: If you arrive at an open intersection at the same time as a car on your right, let that car go first. You can go when it is safe.

questions.question: What does a flashing red light on a traffic signal mean?

options.text: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
The traffic signal is broken.
You do not have to stop completely.
Driving conditions are dangerous.

questions.correctAnswerText: It means the same thing as a stop sign.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light works like a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, check for traffic and pedestrians, and only go when it is safe.

questions.question: When you see a school bus stopped with its stop arm extended, what should you do?

options.text: Come to a complete stop and wait.
Honk before passing the bus on the left.
Continue driving when you think the kids are done exiting.
Pass the bus before its door opens.

questions.correctAnswerText: Come to a complete stop and wait.
questions.explanation: When a school bus has its stop arm extended, you must come to a complete stop. Do not go until the stop arm is pulled back.

questions.question: What should you do at a railroad crossing that has no traffic signals?

options.text: Always come to a complete stop.
Slow down and be ready to stop.
All railroad crossings have signals, so this will never happen.
Speed up to cross the tracks quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: At a railroad crossing without signals, slow down and be ready to stop. Look both ways for trains before crossing. If you see or hear a train, stop a safe distance away and wait for it to pass.

questions.question: If you become stranded in a snowstorm, what should you do?

options.text: Get out of the car and walk for help.
Lie down in your car and sleep.
Walk into the road to get other drivers' attention.
Stay in your car because rescuers are more likely to find you there.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay in your car because rescuers are more likely to find you there.
questions.explanation: If stranded in a snowstorm, stay in your car and wait for help. You are most likely to be found if you stay with your vehicle. It is also unsafe to walk around in a snowstorm.

questions.question: What is a good rule to remember about passing other cars?

options.text: Pass on the right whenever possible.
Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
Get to the front of slow traffic so you can see better.
Always flash lights and honk to tell others you are passing.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive with traffic flow and pass only when needed.
questions.explanation: Every time you pass, the risk of a crash increases. If you drive faster than other cars, you will keep passing. Instead, drive at the same speed as traffic around you, follow the speed limit, and pass only when necessary.

questions.question: What factors affect how much space you need to cross traffic?

options.text: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
The presence of a stop sign.
Using your turn signals.
Cars behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Road conditions, weather, and oncoming traffic.
questions.explanation: The space you need to cross traffic depends on road conditions, weather, and how fast traffic is coming at you.

questions.question: You are in an accident and another person is injured. What should you do?

options.text: Move the injured person away from the scene right away.
Always leave the injured person where they are.
Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
Stay away from the injured person.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not move the injured person unless necessary. Keep them warm and give first aid.
questions.explanation: Do not move an injured person unless you must. Moving them incorrectly can turn minor injuries into serious ones. Keep them warm until help arrives. If there is heavy bleeding, press down on the wound to stop the bleeding.

questions.question: You miss your freeway exit. What should you do?

options.text: Go to the next exit.
Make a U-turn across the median.
Pull onto the shoulder and back up to the exit.
Flag down a police officer to escort you back to your exit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go to the next exit.
questions.explanation: If you miss your exit, take the next one. Do not stop or back up on the highway. Do not cross multiple lanes or turn around at the median. These actions are illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: At a light rail intersection, you should always:

options.text: Look both ways before crossing tracks.
Pay attention and obey all traffic signals.
Share the road with pedestrians and bicyclists.
All of these.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these.
questions.explanation: Never drive around lowered crossing gates. Always look both ways before turning across train tracks. Always obey signs and traffic signals. Trains share the road with cars and bicyclists.

questions.question: When you see flashing lights or hear a siren from an emergency vehicle, you must:

options.text: Slow down until it passes you.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Wave for the emergency vehicle to pass you.
Merge into the right lane and keep driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move to the right side of the road and stop.
questions.explanation: Let any emergency vehicle using flashing lights or a siren pass. You must immediately move to the right side of the road and stop. If you are in an intersection, drive through it first, then stop on the right side.

questions.question: Who must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle by law?

options.text: Anyone under 18 years old
Adult passengers
The driver
Backseat passengers

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone under 18 years old
questions.explanation: Seat belts prevent injury and death in crashes. By law, anyone under 18 must wear a seat belt in a moving vehicle. Everyone should wear a seat belt, no matter their age.

questions.question: Work zone signs mean:

options.text: It is summer.
You must stop and back up immediately.
Driving conditions are difficult.
You should drive faster to get through the work zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: Driving conditions are difficult.
questions.explanation: Work zone signs are orange and show that work is happening on or near the road. Drive carefully when you see these signs.

questions.question: When a car ahead has bright headlights that blind you, you should:

options.text: Use your high beams until the other driver dims theirs.
Flash your lights on and off to warn the driver.
Dim your lights and speed up to pass quickly.
Look toward the right side of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of the road.
questions.explanation: If oncoming headlights are too bright, look away from them toward the right side of the road until the car passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: When a driver behind you wants to pass, you should:

options.text: Speed up.
Keep the same speed.
Slow down to give the other driver room to pass easily.
Change lanes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down to give the other driver room to pass easily.
questions.explanation: Slow down when a driver behind you wants to pass. This creates space in front of your car for them to complete the pass safely and quickly.

questions.question: Motorcycles are allowed:

options.text: In the bicycle lane.
The same full lane width as other vehicles.
Half the width of a lane.
The width of the sidewalk.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same full lane width as other vehicles.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles must use the full lane width like all other vehicles.

questions.question: On slippery roads, you should:

options.text: Slow down.
Drive faster.
Drive at the speed limit with caution.
Never drive faster than 20 mph.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Slow down when you see rain, snow, or sleet. These make roads slippery. When road conditions are poor, safety may require driving slower than the speed limit.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver is behind you, what should you do?

options.text: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
Look at the driver as they pass you.
Speed up while they are passing you.
Block the passing lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move out of the aggressive driver's way.
questions.explanation: If you see an aggressive driver, get out of their way. Do not make eye contact with them. Do not speed up—this may make them angrier and more dangerous.

questions.question: When can you cross a solid yellow line?

options.text: To pass traffic moving in the same direction.
During the day only.
At any time.
When making a turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: When making a turn.
questions.explanation: You can cross broken lines, but not solid lines. You may cross a solid yellow line only when you are turning.

questions.question: When should you increase your following distance?

options.text: When driving behind a large vehicle that blocks your view.
When exiting a highway.
When following a motorcycle.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when behind a large vehicle that blocks your view, in bad weather or heavy traffic, when exiting a highway, when behind a motorcycle or bicycle, and when someone is tailgating you.

questions.question: What should you do if you see an animal on the road?

options.text: No special action is needed.
Honk your horn.
Pass the animal as close as possible.
Be very careful.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be very careful.
questions.explanation: Be very careful when you see an animal on the road. Pass it slowly to avoid scaring it.

questions.question: What should you do before starting the car?

options.text: Make sure only backseat passengers have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only adults have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure only children have buckled their seat belts.
Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure everyone in the car has buckled their seat belt.
questions.explanation: Develop a routine before you start the car. Buckle your own seat belt and make sure all passengers do the same.

questions.question: Who must yield when a driver is turning and a pedestrian is crossing without a traffic light?

options.text: Whoever started moving last.
The driver.
Whoever is slower.
The pedestrian.

questions.correctAnswerText: The driver.
questions.explanation: Drivers must yield to pedestrians crossing at any intersection without a traffic light, whether or not there is a crosswalk.

questions.question: When is it important to slow down?

options.text: On narrow or winding roads.
At intersections or railroad crossings.
When the road is wet or slippery.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Slow down on narrow or winding roads, near intersections, near railroad crossings, on hills, in sharp or blind curves, where there are pedestrians or hazards, and when the road is wet or slippery.

questions.question: What should you do before changing lanes on a highway?

options.text: Honk your horn.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down.
Check your mirrors and blind spots.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check your mirrors and blind spots.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, look in your rearview and side mirrors to see if anyone is passing you. Also look over your shoulder to check your blind spot.

questions.question: What should you do at a flashing yellow light?

options.text: Speed up.
Stop completely.
Turn on your headlights.
Slow down and proceed carefully.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and proceed carefully.
questions.explanation: A flashing yellow light warns of a hazard. Slow down and proceed with caution.

questions.question: What does a speed restriction sign show?

options.text: It can be ignored when it is rainy, snowy, or icy.
It has a triangular shape.
It is blue with black letters.
It shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: It shows a recommended speed for a curve or turn.
questions.explanation: Curve and turn signs often have an advisory speed sign showing the recommended speed for those curves and turns. Even if you feel safe going faster in good weather, never exceed the recommended speed in rain, snow, or ice.

questions.question: You should leave more space than usual when stopping:

options.text: On a hill going upward.
At an intersection.
At a stop sign.
At a toll plaza.

questions.correctAnswerText: On a hill going upward.
questions.explanation: Leave extra space in front of your vehicle when stopped on an uphill slope. If the car ahead rolls backward when traffic starts moving, you will have room to avoid a collision.

questions.question: A solid yellow line on your side of the road means:

options.text: Slow down.
Pass with caution.
Do not pass.
Keep right on hills.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do not pass.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow line next to your lane means you cannot pass other vehicles from your direction.

questions.question: You are waiting in a line of cars at a stop sign. The cars ahead have passed through. There is no traffic crossing. What must you do?

options.text: You can go through the intersection without stopping again.
You must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
You can slowly roll past the stop sign.
You can follow the car ahead without stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop at the stop sign or stop line before going.
questions.explanation: You must always come to a complete stop at a stop sign and check for traffic before proceeding. Do not skip this stop just because other cars are moving.

questions.question: When leaving a highway, when should you slow down?

options.text: On the main road, just before the exit lane.
Once you see a toll booth.
After you move into the exit lane.
When you first see the exit sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: After you move into the exit lane.
questions.explanation: Move into the exit lane first. Then slow down. Do not slow down before you enter the exit lane.

questions.question: Crossbuck signs tell you about:

options.text: Railroad crossings.
School zones.
No passing zones.
Hospitals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: Crossbuck signs warn you that a railroad crossing is ahead. Yield to trains and do not try to drive around the gates.

questions.question: This road sign means:

options.text: No left turn.
No U-turns.
No exit.
No right turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot turn right at this location.

questions.question: This sign means:

options.text: No left turn.
No stopping.
No U-turn.
Detour ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn.
questions.explanation: This sign means you cannot make a U-turn at this location.

questions.question: To help prevent crashes, you should:

options.text: Tell other drivers what you are doing.
Ignore other drivers on the road.
Drive only on side streets and back roads.
Avoid driving during rush hour.

questions.correctAnswerText: Tell other drivers what you are doing.
questions.explanation: Crashes happen when drivers do things that surprise other people. Use your signals when slowing down, stopping, or turning. Use your horn or emergency signals when needed.

questions.question: As a pedestrian, you should:

options.text: Always have the right-of-way over vehicles in a crosswalk.
Never enter a street or crosswalk when cars are coming.
Enter a crosswalk anytime because drivers must stop.
Use crosswalks only when it is convenient.

questions.correctAnswerText: Never enter a street or crosswalk when cars are coming.
questions.explanation: Do not enter a street or crosswalk when vehicles are approaching. Even though pedestrians have the right-of-way in crosswalks, a car that is close may not be able to stop in time.

questions.question: A speed limit sign shows:

options.text: Only a suggested speed.
The exact speed you must drive to avoid a ticket.
The fastest safe speed when road and weather are good.
The fastest safe speed in all conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fastest safe speed when road and weather are good.
questions.explanation: A speed limit sign shows the highest legal speed for that road. When conditions are poor, you should drive slower than the posted limit.
